title: Adaptive Windows, Foldables, ChromeOS, and Input

scout.purpose: Master adaptive windows, foldables, chromeos, and input through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend adaptive windows, foldables, chromeos, and input.

blocks.text: Design for the current window, not a phone or tablet label. Window size can change through rotation, split screen, desktop resizing, fold and unfold, external displays, or freeform windows. Use adaptive breakpoints and available space to change navigation, panes, and content density while preserving task continuity. Folding features describe occlusion or posture when relevant, but a hinge is not always a divider. Avoid orientation locks and device-name branches.

blocks.text: ChromeOS and large screens add resizable windows, keyboard, mouse, trackpad, hover, right click, drag, selection, and multiple simultaneous app instances. Touch remains important. Make every operation keyboard reachable, preserve focus visibly, use semantic shortcuts, support wheel and pointer precision, and avoid gesture-only commands. State must survive resizing and configuration without resetting work. Camera, sensors, telephony, and portrait assumptions need capability checks and useful alternatives.

blocks.text: Test compact through expanded windows, tabletop posture, occluding hinge, external display, density, text scaling, RTL, multi-window, resume after process death, keyboard-only, mouse, touch, stylus, and screen reader. Use resizable emulators and physical foldables where possible. Screenshot tests cover layout but not focus or task continuity. Measure performance at large content areas. A successful adaptive app adds value with space rather than merely stretching controls.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

trap_check.mistake: Checking smallestScreenWidth once at startup misses live window resizing, multi-window, fold posture, and external-display changes.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Adapt a master-detail workflow across compact, tabletop, expanded desktop, keyboard, pointer, drag, and process recreation with continuity and accessibility.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: Why is window size more useful than device category?
recall.answer: The app renders into a changeable window whose size and features may not match a fixed phone, tablet, or foldable label.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
